meta.scope: Taiwan Batch 12 — Broad densification pass. Strengthens cross-cluster connections: whole-of-society / civil-defense resilience, semiconductor talent & STEM pipeline, LNG / energy-security (linking to ART US purchase commitments), dual-use industrial edges, fiscal/revenue links to chips and defense, and additional relational indicators that tighten the triangle and domestic clusters. Explicit referenced_by lists throughout.
meta.strategy_note: User request to densify everywhere and look for more connections. This batch prioritises nodes that create edges *between* existing clusters (defense ↔ semiconductor, energy ↔ ART, talent ↔ industrial, resilience ↔ demographic) rather than isolated leaves.

candidates.title: Whole-of-Society Defense Resilience Committee / All-Out Defense Mobilization statistics
candidates.publisher: Presidential Office / Ministry of National Defense (All-Out Defense Mobilization Agency) / related agencies
candidates.description: Institutional and statistical products of the Whole-of-Society Defense Resilience Committee (established 2024) and the All-Out Defense Mobilization Agency. Tracks civil-defense personnel registration (recently >3.2 million), training slots, strategic material and food reserves (rice stockpiles exceeding national-security standards), and multi-sector resilience planning (energy, medical, information, critical supply).
referenced_by: National Defense Report and asymmetric special budgets
candidates.notes: Key bridging node between the pure military cluster and the broader demographic, energy and social clusters. Makes ‘resilience’ statistically visible rather than purely rhetorical.

candidates.title: Civil defense personnel registration and training statistics
candidates.publisher: All-Out Defense Mobilization Agency / National Audit Office reporting
candidates.description: Quantitative series on the number of registered civil-defense personnel, training completions, multi-category registrations, and related mobilisation readiness indicators.
candidates.notes: Manpower-side densification of the resilience cluster. Links directly to the demographic constraints already mapped.

candidates.title: Semiconductor and high-tech talent / STEM workforce pipeline statistics
candidates.publisher: National Science and Technology Council / Ministry of Education / industry-academia programmes / National Applied Research Laboratories (semiconductor center)
candidates.description: Statistics and programme data on the supply of semiconductor and STEM talent — university and graduate output, industry-academia collaboration places, foreign student / work-study inflows into electronics manufacturing, and high-end R&D training capacity (e.g. National Semiconductor Center annual trainee volumes). Persistent shortages are a recurrent official and industry theme.
referenced_by: R&D expenditure and science-park employment statistics
Industrial Innovation Act and talent-policy documents
candidates.notes: Critical constraint node. Tightens edges between the education, labour, R&D and semiconductor clusters and explains part of the wage premium and dual-structure pattern.

candidates.title: LNG imports, natural-gas supply and energy-security statistics
candidates.publisher: Energy Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs
candidates.description: Statistics on LNG import volumes, supplier composition (Qatar, Australia, United States, others), gas consumption (power generation dominant), and related energy-security indicators. AI-driven electricity demand from semiconductors and data centres is explicitly linked to rising gas requirements in recent official commentary.
referenced_by: Energy Statistics Handbook and electricity generation mix
US–Taiwan ART purchase commitments (LNG and energy equipment)
Industrial production and AI-demand concentration nodes
candidates.notes: High-value cross-cluster node. Links energy security to (1) the semiconductor/AI electricity load, (2) the ART’s large US LNG purchase pledges, and (3) resilience planning. Strengthens the energy arm of the triangle.

candidates.title: US–Taiwan ART / related commitments on energy and critical-equipment purchases
candidates.publisher: AIT–TECRO / USTR / Taiwan official fact sheets
candidates.description: Specific quantitative commitments embedded in the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade and associated understandings for long-term purchases of US LNG, crude oil, civil aircraft, power equipment and related items. Provides a concrete commercial edge from the economic-security architecture into Taiwan’s energy-import statistics.
candidates.notes: Direct quantitative bridge between Batch 8 (ART) and the energy-security cluster.

candidates.title: Dual-use and defense-relevant industrial statistics (shipbuilding, electronics, materials)
candidates.publisher: Ministry of National Defense / Ministry of Economic Affairs / related industrial agencies
candidates.description: Statistical and programme traces of industrial capacity that serves both commercial high-tech (especially electronics and advanced materials) and defence requirements (indigenous shipbuilding, missiles, C4ISR components). Captures the overlap zone between the semiconductor/electronics cluster and the defence-industrial cluster.
referenced_by: Indigenous naval shipbuilding and defence-industry statistics
candidates.notes: Explicit dual-use edge. Prevents the military and semiconductor clusters from remaining siloed.

candidates.title: Fiscal and tax revenue links to semiconductor / electronics sector
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Finance / DGBAS / National Taxation Bureau related
candidates.description: Available statistical indicators of the contribution of the electronics / semiconductor sector to corporate tax, business tax and overall fiscal revenue, and of the fiscal cost of Industrial Innovation Act / Chip Act incentives. Links the high-profit semiconductor cluster to public-finance capacity (including rising defence budgets).
referenced_by: National accounts and government finance statistics
candidates.notes: Fiscal densification. Makes the public-finance consequences of the semiconductor boom (and its tax incentives) visible and connectable to the defence-spending trajectory.

candidates.title: Cybersecurity, information resilience and C4ISR statistics / programmes
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Digital Affairs / Ministry of National Defense / related agencies
candidates.description: Programme and statistical traces of cybersecurity, critical-information-infrastructure protection, and military C4ISR resilience efforts. Appears in special-budget lines, Whole-of-Society Resilience workstreams, and digital-affairs reporting.
candidates.notes: Digital-security bridge between the pure defence cluster and the digital-economy / ICT nodes.

candidates.title: Strategic material and food-reserve statistics
candidates.publisher: All-Out Defense Mobilization Agency / Ministry of Agriculture / related agencies
candidates.description: Statistics on public grain (rice) reserves, strategic material stockpiles, and related readiness indicators that form part of the whole-of-society resilience framework. Recent rice reserves have exceeded the formal national-security standard.
candidates.notes: Material-side densification of the resilience cluster. Links agriculture and food-security nodes to the defence-mobilisation architecture.

candidates.title: Taiwan cross-cluster densification meta-node (resilience–talent–energy–dual-use–fiscal)
candidates.publisher: Derived from MND, NSTC, Energy Administration, MOF, MODA and related sources
candidates.description: Meta-node that records the intentional densification of edges among previously somewhat separate clusters: whole-of-society resilience ↔ military, semiconductor talent ↔ industrial production & R&D, LNG/energy security ↔ ART commitments & AI electricity load, dual-use industry ↔ defence + electronics, fiscal revenue ↔ semiconductor profits & defence budgets. Serves as an explicit reminder to the force layout that these domains are now more densely interlinked.
referenced_by: All detailed densification nodes in this batch
Earlier semiconductor, defence, energy, demographic and triangle meta-nodes
candidates.notes: Book-keeping and structural node. Helps the force mechanisms treat the newly strengthened cross-links as first-class rather than incidental.
